name: High-dose CISplatin plus concurrent radiation (definitive or postoperative)
disease: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

biomarkers.note: For p16-positive (HPV-associated) oropharyngeal cancer, p16/HPV status is strongly prognostic but is NOT a dose gate for this regimen; the concurrent high-dose cisplatin schedule is unchanged. RTOG 1016 and De-ESCALATE established that concurrent high-dose cisplatin was superior to cetuximab in p16-positive oropharyngeal cancer (Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers, algorithm HN region; DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 23, line 62062).

lineOfTherapy: primary concurrent chemoradiation for locoregionally advanced disease (definitive), or concurrent with postoperative radiation for high-risk pathologic features (adjuvant); not line-scoped

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: locoregionally advanced SCCHN treated with definitive radiation, OR postoperative high-risk pathology (positive margin and/or extranodal extension)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: Chapter 23, lines 58086 to 58088 (definitive) and lines 58225 to 58240 (postoperative RTOG 9501 / EORTC 22931 combined analysis: positive mucosal margin and extracapsular spread)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate renal function and hydration tolerance for high-dose cisplatin; no severe pre-existing ototoxicity or neuropathy
eligibilityCriteria.locator: Chapter 23, lines 58194 to 58200 (cisplatin toxicity: renal, otologic, neurologic)

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
provenance.locator: Definitive concurrent schedule: single-agent cisplatin every 3 weeks at 100 mg/m2, 2 to 3 cycles depending on fractionation (algorithm HN region, lines 1281, 3976, 4332); Discussion, high-dose cisplatin 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks for up to three cycles (line 8778); postoperative concurrent, cisplatin 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks for three doses (line 8287)

drugs.notes: Source: cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV every 21 days concurrent with radiation, for a total of 3 cycles (2 to 3 depending on fractionation). Corroborated DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 23, lines 58086 to 58088 (100 mg per m2 every 3 weeks for a total of 3 cycles) and formulary line 14827 (Head and neck cancer: 100 mg/m2 IV). ISMP tall-man. No lifetime cumulative cap for cisplatin; monitor for nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy and ensure pre- and post-hydration.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis (high emetic risk)
premedications.notes: Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 is highly emetogenic; high-emetic-risk prophylaxis indicated. Confirm exact institutional antiemetic tier.

premedications.name: Hydration
premedications.notes: Aggressive IV pre- and post-hydration to reduce nephrotoxicity, per cisplatin standard of care (DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 23, lines 58194 to 58200).

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: high emetic risk (cisplatin-containing); prophylaxis required. Confirm exact institutional/guideline tier.
Nephroprotection: mandatory IV hydration and electrolyte (Mg, K) repletion with each dose.

monitoring: Renal function (creatinine/GFR) and electrolytes (Mg, K, Na) before each cycle - cisplatin nephrotoxicity
Audiometry / ototoxicity assessment (high-frequency hearing loss, tinnitus) - cisplatin
Peripheral neuropathy assessment before each cycle - cisplatin

doseModificationRules.condition: rising creatinine / falling GFR or significant ototoxicity or grade 2+ neuropathy
doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Consider dose reduction, delay, or switch to carboplatin-based or weekly schedule per clinical judgement. Physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Chapter 23, lines 58086 to 58088 (definitive high-dose cisplatin 100 mg/m2 q3wk x3), lines 58225 to 58240 (postoperative concurrent cisplatin, RTOG 9501 / EORTC 22931), formulary line 14827 (head and neck cancer cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV)

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
guideline.locator: Concurrent single-agent cisplatin every 3 weeks at 100 mg/m2, 2 to 3 cycles (algorithm HN region, lines 1281/3976/4332); Discussion lines 8287 (postoperative), 8778 (definitive preferred)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for high-dose CISplatin concurrent with radiation in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Setting: definitive concurrent chemoradiation for locoregionally advanced disease, or concurrent with postoperative radiation for high-risk pathology (positive margin and/or extranodal extension). Sites served (squamous histology): oral cavity (#32), tongue (#33), lip (#34), oropharyngeal (#35), HPV-positive oropharyngeal (#36, where p16/HPV is prognostic only and does not alter dosing), hypopharyngeal (#38), laryngeal (#39), and sinonasal (#41); nasopharyngeal (#37) is covered by the dedicated NPC protocols and salivary (#40) is not covered. Dose fully grounded: CISplatin 100 mg/m2 IV every 21 days for 3 cycles concurrent with radiation (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) 2.2026 algorithm HN region and Discussion lines 8287/8778; DeVita 12th ed. Chapter 23 lines 58086 to 58088 and formulary line 14827). ISMP tall-man applied. Cisplatin has NO lifetime cumulative cap; nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neuropathy monitoring plus mandatory hydration are specified in clearanceChecks and monitoring. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
